name: Soprano Ice laser

card.summary: A diode-type hair-removal system marketed as lower-pain; one small study of the triple-wavelength Platinum model in darker skin.
card.note: Little independent evidence on the pain claim was found.

quick.overview:
Soprano Ice is a hair-removal laser line from Alma Lasers. The Soprano Ice Platinum combines 755, 810 and 1064 nm wavelengths in one device.

One published study evaluated the triple-wavelength Platinum for hair reduction in skin types IV to V.
quick.mechanism: Like other hair-removal lasers it targets melanin in hair follicles by selective photothermolysis, with cooling to protect the skin. Combining wavelengths is described as an approach to treat a range of skin types.
quick.risks: General laser hair-removal risks apply: redness, swelling, burns and pigment changes. Specific data on pain reduction versus other devices were not found.

lead: Soprano Ice is a line of hair-removal lasers from Alma Lasers, marketed for lower-discomfort treatment. The Soprano Ice Platinum emits three wavelengths, 755, 810 and 1064 nm, in one device [1]. People use laser hair removal to get long-term reduction of facial or body hair, so the skin looks smooth and shaving or waxing is needed less often [2].

Laser hair removal works by selective photothermolysis: melanin in the hair absorbs the light and heats the follicle's stem cells, damaging them [2]. The three wavelengths correspond to alexandrite (755 nm), diode (810 nm) and Nd:YAG (1064 nm) lasers, which Wikipedia associates with all skin types, pale to medium skin and dark skin respectively [2]. A 2021 paper in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology reported on the Platinum's efficacy and safety for hair reduction in Fitzpatrick skin types IV to V [1].
infobox: At least eight, 3-8 weeks apart (laser hair removal generally) [2]
Contact cooling commonly used to reduce pain and side effects [2]

paras: Melanin is the main chromophore: eumelanin in brown or black hair absorbs laser energy, while white, grey, light blonde and red hair respond poorly [2]. Lasers affect only follicles in the active growth phase, which is why several sessions are needed, and touch-ups may be required later [2].

Contact cooling, cryogen spray or forced cold air allows higher fluence and reduces pain and side effects, especially in darker skin; numbing cream is also available [2]. Common short-lived effects include itching, redness and swelling lasting two or three days, and rarer ones include burns, pigment change and infection [2]. In the US the FDA approves lasers for permanent hair reduction, meaning long-term reduction rather than complete removal [2].

A study of the Soprano Ice Platinum in skin types IV to V was published in 2021 [1]. For laser hair removal in general, Wikipedia cites a randomized trial reporting 69.2% reduction with a diode laser at 12 months and a 2006 review reporting six-month reductions of about 68.8% for alexandrite and 71.7% for diode lasers [2].

The device is marketed as a lower-pain hair-removal system; no published trial comparing its pain levels with other systems was found. Wikipedia notes that cooling is the method generally used by lasers to cut pain [2].

refs.title: Efficacy and safety of triple wavelength laser hair reduction in skin types IV to V

chain: Laser light absorbed by melanin in the hair
Follicle stem cells are heated and damaged
Long-term reduction of regrowing hair after a course of sessions
angle.text: Sessions with a laser like the Soprano Ice reduce hair growth on treated areas, leaving smoother skin with less regrowth. Most people need at least eight sessions spaced weeks apart, and men's facial hair often needs more [2].
